Why This Role Matters

Every day, the world's most mission-critical companies — banks, hospitals, governments, and Fortune 500 enterprises — run on Salesforce. And every day, the teams behind those orgs face a choice: move fast or stay safe. At Flosum, we refuse that tradeoff. As the only 100% Salesforce-native DevSecOps, data, and security platform, we empower teams to ship fearlessly, recover instantly, and govern with confidence — all without leaving the platform they love.

We're looking for a visionary product leader who sees what's possible when innovation and trust live in the same place. Someone who wants to leave a fingerprint on an entire ecosystem.

The Opportunity

This is more than a product role — it's a chance to architect the operating system for the modern Salesforce enterprise. You will own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for a platform that touches release managers at sunrise, developers at midnight, and CISOs every minute in between. You'll lead a passionate team of product managers, partner shoulder-to-shoulder with brilliant engineers, and sit at the table with customers solving problems that matter — from accelerating releases by 10x to recovering an org in minutes after a catastrophic event.

If you've ever wanted to build the category-defining product in Salesforce DevOps, this is your moment.

What You'll Do

  • Set the North Star. Craft a bold, multi-year product vision that anticipates where Salesforce — and the AI-powered enterprise — is heading next, from Agentforce to Data Cloud and beyond.
  • Build the team that builds the future. Recruit, mentor, and inspire a world-class product organization across DevOps, data management, and security — a team people fight to join and never want to leave.
  • Obsess over customers. Sit with admins, developers, release managers, and security leaders. Understand their 2 a.m. anxieties and their 10 a.m. ambitions. Turn those insights into products they'll champion.
  • Ship things that matter. Drive the full lifecycle — from messy whiteboard to flawless launch — for capabilities like Git-based version control, AI-assisted code review, intelligent backup & recovery, and zero-trust security.
  • Stay ahead of the platform. Turn every Salesforce release into an opportunity, not a fire drill, ensuring Flosum is always first and always native.
  • Win the category. Outthink and outmaneuver every competitor by knowing the market deeper than anyone else and telling a story only Flosum can tell.
  • Be a force multiplier. Partner with marketing, sales, success, and AppExchange & SI partners to turn great products into great businesses.

Requirements

Who You Are

  • A product leader with 10+ years of experience and the scars and wins to prove it — including 3+ years building and leading PM teams.
  • A Salesforce native at heart — you dream in metadata, you've debugged a deployment at midnight, and you know why governor limits exist (and how to live with them).
  • A builder who has shipped DevOps, ALM, data protection, or security products that customers genuinely love.
  • A strategist who can paint the 5-year picture and an operator who can ship next Tuesday.
  • A storyteller comfortable in front of a single customer, a packed room, an analyst, or a board.
  • A magnet for talent and a champion of the people you lead.

Bonus Superpowers

  • Deep fluency in Git, CI/CD (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps), and modern developer workflows.
  • Experience with backup, archival, sandbox seeding, and data masking at enterprise scale.
  • Battle-tested in regulated environments — SOC 2, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR.
  • A point of view on how AI will reshape the Salesforce admin and developer experience — and the chops to ship it.
  • Salesforce certifications, an engineering background, or an MBA that sharpens your edge.

What Success Looks Like

  • One year from now, you will have published a roadmap the entire ecosystem talks about, built a team that's the envy of the industry, and shipped releases that move ARR, expand customer relationships, and cement Flosum as the undisputed leader on the AppExchange. Five years from now, you'll look back at a category you helped define — and an enterprise software movement you helped lead.

    If you're ready to do the most meaningful work of your career, we're ready to build it with you.

Every day, the world's most mission-critical companies — banks, hospitals, governments, and Fortune 500 enterprises — run on Salesforce. And every day, the teams behind those orgs face a choice: move fast or stay safe. At Flosum, we refuse that tradeoff. As the only 100% Salesforce-native DevSecOps, data, and security platform, we empower teams to ship fearlessly, recover instantly, and govern with confidence — all without leaving the platform they love.

We're looking for a visionary product leader who sees what's possible when innovation and trust live in the same place. Someone who wants to leave a fingerprint on an entire ecosystem.

The Opportunity

This is more than a product role — it's a chance to architect the operating system for the modern Salesforce enterprise. You will own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for a platform that touches release managers at sunrise, developers at midnight, and CISOs every minute in between. You'll lead a passionate team of product managers, partner shoulder-to-shoulder with brilliant engineers, and sit at the table with customers solving problems that matter — from accelerating releases by 10x to recovering an org in minutes after a catastrophic event.

If you've ever wanted to build the category-defining product in Salesforce DevOps, this is your moment.

What You'll Do

  • Set the North Star. Craft a bold, multi-year product vision that anticipates where Salesforce — and the AI-powered enterprise — is heading next, from Agentforce to Data Cloud and beyond.
  • Build the team that builds the future. Recruit, mentor, and inspire a world-class product organization across DevOps, data management, and security — a team people fight to join and never want to leave.
  • Obsess over customers. Sit with admins, developers, release managers, and security leaders. Understand their 2 a.m. anxieties and their 10 a.m. ambitions. Turn those insights into products they'll champion.
  • Ship things that matter. Drive the full lifecycle — from messy whiteboard to flawless launch — for capabilities like Git-based version control, AI-assisted code review, intelligent backup & recovery, and zero-trust security.
  • Stay ahead of the platform. Turn every Salesforce release into an opportunity, not a fire drill, ensuring Flosum is always first and always native.
  • Win the category. Outthink and outmaneuver every competitor by knowing the market deeper than anyone else and telling a story only Flosum can tell.
  • Be a force multiplier. Partner with marketing, sales, success, and AppExchange & SI partners to turn great products into great businesses.

Requirements

Who You Are

  • A product leader with 10+ years of experience and the scars and wins to prove it — including 3+ years building and leading PM teams.
  • A Salesforce native at heart — you dream in metadata, you've debugged a deployment at midnight, and you know why governor limits exist (and how to live with them).
  • A builder who has shipped DevOps, ALM, data protection, or security products that customers genuinely love.
  • A strategist who can paint the 5-year picture and an operator who can ship next Tuesday.
  • A storyteller comfortable in front of a single customer, a packed room, an analyst, or a board.
  • A magnet for talent and a champion of the people you lead.

Bonus Superpowers

  • Deep fluency in Git, CI/CD (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps), and modern developer workflows.
  • Experience with backup, archival, sandbox seeding, and data masking at enterprise scale.
  • Battle-tested in regulated environments — SOC 2, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR.
  • A point of view on how AI will reshape the Salesforce admin and developer experience — and the chops to ship it.
  • Salesforce certifications, an engineering background, or an MBA that sharpens your edge.

What Success Looks Like

  • One year from now, you will have published a roadmap the entire ecosystem talks about, built a team that's the envy of the industry, and shipped releases that move ARR, expand customer relationships, and cement Flosum as the undisputed leader on the AppExchange. Five years from now, you'll look back at a category you helped define — and an enterprise software movement you helped lead.

    If you're ready to do the most meaningful work of your career, we're ready to build it with you.

raw.description:
Outbound Sales Development Representative – Remote

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Business Hours

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a highly driven and results-oriented Outbound Sales Development Representative (SDR) to help build and scale their outbound sales function.

This is not a lead-following role.

You’ll be responsible for building your own prospect lists, executing multi-channel outbound campaigns, booking qualified meetings, and maintaining a healthy sales pipeline. Success in this role comes from proactively creating opportunities through cold calling, cold emailing, and LinkedIn outreach—not waiting for inbound leads.

If you’re competitive, resilient, and thrive on opening doors with decision-makers, this role offers significant growth potential within a fast-growing marketing agency serving the home services industry.

What You’ll Own

Outbound Prospecting & Lead Generation

  • Execute high-volume outbound prospecting through:
    • Cold calls
    • Cold emails
    • LinkedIn outreach
  • Identify and engage decision-makers within target companies.
  • Build and maintain your own prospecting lists using sales tools and research.
  • Generate qualified opportunities for the closing team.
  • Maintain consistent daily outreach activity across multiple channels.

Appointment Setting & Pipeline Development

  • Book qualified meetings with prospective clients.
  • Qualify prospects using established criteria before scheduling appointments.
  • Improve meeting attendance through effective follow-up and communication.
  • Maintain a healthy pipeline of opportunities.
  • Partner closely with Account Executives to ensure smooth handoffs.

Objection Handling & Sales Execution

  • Handle objections confidently and professionally.
  • Navigate gatekeepers and decision-makers effectively.
  • Build rapport and communicate value quickly.
  • Continuously improve scripts, messaging, and outreach strategies.
  • Test new approaches to increase conversion rates.

CRM & Sales Operations

  • Maintain accurate CRM records and pipeline updates.
  • Log call notes, outreach activities, and follow-up tasks.
  • Track opportunity stages and sales activity.
  • Ensure CRM hygiene and reporting accuracy.

Reporting & Performance

  • Report daily and weekly outreach activity.
  • Track meetings booked and pipeline performance.
  • Monitor key sales metrics and identify improvement opportunities.
  • Take ownership of personal performance and quota attainment.

What Success Looks Like

  • Consistently books qualified meetings.
  • Maintains high outbound activity across multiple channels.
  • Achieves strong meeting attendance rates.
  • Generates a predictable pipeline of sales opportunities.
  • Maintains clean CRM records and accurate reporting.
  • Contributes directly to business growth through outbound sales.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You genuinely enjoy outbound prospecting.
  • You’re motivated by competition and measurable goals.
  • You thrive on opening conversations with new prospects.
  • You remain persistent and positive after rejection.
  • You take ownership of your performance without constant supervision.
  • You continuously improve your outreach strategy based on results.

Required Experience & Skills

Experience

  • Proven experience as:
    • Sales Development Representative (SDR)
    • Appointment Setter
    • Business Development Representative (BDR)
    • Outbound Sales Representative
  • Demonstrated success achieving or exceeding outbound sales targets.
  • Experience executing multi-channel outbound prospecting through:
    • Cold calling
    • Cold emailing
    • LinkedIn outreach
  • Strong objection-handling and prospecting skills.
  • Proven ability to book qualified meetings with decision-makers.
  • Experience maintaining CRM accuracy and managing pipelines.
  • Excellent written and spoken English communication skills.
  • Strong organizational and time-management abilities.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to provide measurable performance metrics such as:
    • Meetings booked
    • Show-up rates
    • Call volume
    • Conversion rates
    • Quota attainment

Nice to Have

  • Experience selling to U.S.-based clients.
  • Background in:
    • B2B sales
    • Marketing services
    • Agency sales
  • Experience selling into the home services industry.
  • Experience using:
    • Salesforce
    • HubSpot
    • Similar CRM platforms
  • Familiarity with:
    • CloudTalk
    • Aircall
    • Similar dialers
  • Experience using LinkedIn Sales Navigator.
  • Exposure to AI tools, SaaS, or startup environments.

Tech Stack

  • Salesforce
  • HubSpot
  • LinkedIn Sales Navigator
  • CloudTalk
  • Aircall
  • Google Workspace
  • Microsoft Office
  • AI productivity tools (ChatGPT or similar)

What a Typical Day Looks Like

  • Review your pipeline and prioritize follow-ups.
  • Conduct cold calls and outbound prospecting.
  • Send personalized cold emails and LinkedIn messages.
  • Qualify prospects and overcome objections.
  • Schedule meetings for the sales team.
  • Update CRM records and pipeline stages.
  • Review outreach metrics and refine messaging.
  • Collaborate with the closing team to ensure smooth handoffs.

In short: You’ll build pipeline from scratch by prospecting, qualifying decision-makers, booking meetings, and creating consistent outbound opportunities that drive business growth.

Key Metrics for Success (KPIs)

  • Outbound calls completed.
  • Cold emails and LinkedIn outreach activity.
  • Qualified meetings booked.
  • Meeting attendance (show-up) rate.
  • Lead-to-meeting conversion rate.
  • Pipeline growth and opportunity creation.
  • CRM accuracy and activity tracking.
  • Quota attainment.

Why This Role Stands Out

  • High ownership over outbound sales and pipeline generation.
  • Opportunity to shape and grow the outbound sales function.
  • Direct impact on company revenue and growth.
  • Fully remote work environment.
  • Performance-driven culture with significant career advancement opportunities.
  • Career progression into:
    • Senior SDR
    • Business Development Manager
    • Account Executive
    • Sales Manager

Interview Process

  1. Application Review
  2. Spark Hire Intro Video (3–5 minutes)
  3. Client Interview
  4. Offer & Onboarding

What Happens After You Apply

After submitting your application, you’ll receive an email invitation from Spark Hire to record a short 3–5 minute Intro Video. This is the first step in our hiring process and can be completed whenever it’s convenient for you.

Instead of multiple initial screening calls, you’ll have one opportunity to introduce yourself, discuss your outbound sales experience, and explain how you’ve built prospect lists, handled cold calling, managed objection handling, and consistently booked qualified meetings. You’ll also have the opportunity to highlight your outbound performance metrics, CRM experience, and ability to work independently in a target-driven environment. Your video will be reviewed by the hiring team before moving to the client interview.

You can record your video as many times as you’d like before submitting it—only your final version will be reviewed.

Please keep an eye on both your inbox and spam folder for your Spark Hire invitation after applying.

Apply Now

If you’re passionate about outbound sales, enjoy creating opportunities from scratch, and thrive in a performance-driven environment, we’d love to hear from you. Apply today and help drive business growth through high-quality outbound prospecting and lead generation.

Sales Engineering | United States (Remote) — Pacific, Mountain or Central Region

You'll be the technical lead in Alkira's largest enterprise deals — in the room with network architects and infrastructure directors, owning the technical side of the deal from first conversation through POC to close.

This is a pre-sales engineering role. You'll partner directly with an Account Manager on strategy and carry real influence over what we build next — our Product team treats SE field feedback as a primary input to the roadmap.

Location: Remote, US. Candidates should reside in the Pacific, Mountain or Central time zone for territory coverage.

Travel: approximately 25%, including regional air travel as needed. Please discuss the specifics for this position with the recruiter.

What you'll do

  • Present and demo the Alkira platform to technical decision makers, from engineer to CIO
  • Clearly articulate the Alkira value proposition and have a sound understanding of market, industry and competitive landscape
  • Partner with Alkira Account Managers to understand customer requirements and pain points. Assist with any technical asks from customers and help respond to RFP/RFIs
  • Scope, run and win Proof of Concepts end to end
  • Assist customers with design and deployment based on best practices
  • Work with Alkira Product Management team to provide feedback on upcoming features from the customer's lens

What you need

  • 8+ years in a customer-facing pre-sales engineering role — Sales Engineer, Systems Engineer, Solutions Consultant or Solutions Architect — ideally at a networking or security vendor, cloud provider, channel partner, or consultancy
  • Strong networking fundamentals – Everything below builds on this, and it is not negotiable
  • Deep expertise in routing protocols and technologies, including BGP, OSPF, and static routing, with hands-on experience in route policy design, route redistribution, filtering, and traffic engineering
  • Understanding of network virtualization and software-defined networking, including VRFs, multi-tenant network architectures, SD-WAN, and the encapsulation protocols used to build overlays at scale (GRE, VXLAN, GENEVE and similar)
  • Hands-on experience with IPsec VPNs, encryption standards, NAT, and secure connectivity architectures
  • Good understanding of how enterprises extend cloud connectivity using a variety of Networking Technologies (i.e. Cloud On-Ramps, SD-WAN and IPsec)
  • Experience in large-scale enterprise network design and deployment experience across data center, WAN and hybrid/multi-cloud
  • A deep understanding of network services — DNS, DHCP, load balancing, traffic inspection and similar
  • The ability to troubleshoot live, in front of a customer, across routing, security and cloud domains
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, and comfort presenting and demoing to customers in person – In this role you are the technical credibility of the company

Strongly preferred

  • Understanding of cloud networking constructs across AWS, Azure, and GCP (e.g., VPCs/VNets, Transit Gateway, Virtual WAN, Cloud Router, peering, and hybrid connectivity such as Direct Connect and ExpressRoute)
  • Network security expertise, including firewalls (e.g., Palo Alto Networks, Fortinet, Check Point), firewall policy design, service insertion/chaining, and Zero Trust principles
  • Relevant technical certifications (e.g., CCNP/CCIE, AWS Advanced Networking, Azure Network Engineer, PCNSE)

  • BA/BS/MS in a technical field

About Alkira

Alkira, a Lumen Connect® solution, is building the future of enterprise networking: one programmable platform to connect, secure, and operate every cloud, site, partner, data center, and AI workload.

Founded by Amir and Atif Khan, the creators of Viptela and pioneers of the SD-WAN market, Alkira was built to radically simplify how enterprises deploy and manage network infrastructure. Today, as part of Lumen, we are bringing that cloud-native operating model to a global network foundation trusted by the world's largest enterprises.

Our platform helps customers move faster without managing hardware, stitching together providers, or operating fragmented cloud networks. Teams can build and scale connectivity on demand, apply consistent security and segmentation, and gain visibility across distributed environments from one place.

At Alkira, you'll help shape the next chapter of networking: cloud-like consumption, private-network performance, and total control across the enterprise. We move fast, solve hard problems, and build technology that changes how global businesses connect.

Join us and help build the future of networking.

$200,000.00 - $300,000.00/yr

The range reflects the cost of labor across multiple U.S. geographic markets, and a candidate hired outside the primary market for this role may be compensated at a different rate. The role is eligible for our full benefits package.

title: Solution Architect - Security
description: Telarus is the largest privately held technology services distributor in North America.

raw.title: Solution Architect - Security
raw.excerpt: Telarus is the largest privately held technology services distributor in North America.
raw.description:
Telarus is the largest privately held technology services distributor in North America. We put 400+ supplier relationships: Cybersecurity, CX, SD-WAN/SASE, Cloud, and AI: behind a network of Technology Advisors, MSPs, and VARs who sell to everyone from mid-market to Fortune 500.

This role is the security brain those advisors call when the deal gets real. You are not a demo jockey, and you are not a badge on a slide. You are the architect who walks into a CISO conversation on a partner's behalf, runs the discovery, designs the answer, and helps close the business.

Must have experience being customer-facing for technology sales.

WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

Security is a fast-moving, consultative product — and it is the one where end customers need real help. Deals stall when nobody in the room can hold a credible conversation about risk, controls, frameworks, and what happens at 2 a.m. when the ransomware note appears.

Your job is to make sure that never happens. Every security opportunity in your book should move faster, land bigger, and close cleaner because you were on it.

WHAT YOU WILL OWN

1. Revenue — you carry a number

  • Own influenced security revenue against a quota. This is a performance role with variable comp tied to what you close, not to how many calls you attended.
  • Build and work your own pipeline as you generate opportunities via Advisors. Sit with and help them grow their base, and create opportunities that did not exist before you got there — do not wait for the queue to feed you. The good news: You are not cold-calling.
  • Drive deals to close: multi-thread into the customer, handle objections, build the business case, and stay on it through signature and provisioning.
  • Forecast honestly and manage your pipeline hygiene in Salesforce. We would rather hear bad news early than good news late.

2. Architecture — you design the answer

  • Lead discovery on the partner's behalf: current state, risk posture, compliance drivers, incident history, budget reality, and who actually signs.
  • Design solutions across the full stack — identity and access, network and edge (SASE/SSE/ZTNA), endpoint and XDR, SIEM/SOC and MDR, email and collaboration security, data protection and DLP, cloud posture (CSPM/CNAPP), OT/IoT, offensive testing, and GRC.
  • Translate frameworks into buying decisions — NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CIS, CMMC/DFARS, PCI DSS, HIPAA, SOX, and the state privacy patchwork — and tie controls to the customer's actual exposure and cyber insurance requirements.
  • Run supplier selection with intellectual honesty. Recommend the right fit from our portfolio, not the one that is easiest to quote.
  • Know where your edges are. Spot the cloud, network, CX, or AI attach and pull in the right teammate instead of guessing.

3. Enablement — you make the channel dangerous

  • Train and evangelize advisors and internal employees: whiteboard sessions, webinars, roadshows, mainstage and breakout content at Telarus events.
  • Build reusable assets — battle cards, discovery guides, reference architectures, objection-handling playbooks — so your expertise scales past the calls you personally take.
  • Be a public voice. Podcasts, panels, LinkedIn, industry groups. We want a name that partners ask for.

4. Relationships — you are the connective tissue

  • Own working relationships with supplier channel managers and supplier SEs. Know who to call to get a deal unstuck, a POC scheduled, or pricing sharpened.
  • Maintain deep proficiency in emerging security products, threat trends, and attacker TTPs. This category reinvents itself every 18 months.
  • Partner with Telarus field sales, other engineers, and leadership.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

  • First 30 days: You know our security portfolio cold, you have met your top supplier contacts, and you are shadowing and then leading live partner calls.
  • First 60 days: You are running discovery solo, you have helped an Advisor create opportunities, and you have delivered your first advisor training.
  • First 90 days: You have a real pipeline you built, closed business on the board, and advisors in your region asking for you by name.
  • First 12 months: You are at or over quota, you have published reusable enablement that the whole SE org uses, and you have added an industry-leading certification.

WHAT YOU NEED — SECURITY DEPTH

These are hard requirements. We will test them in the interview.

  • 8+ years in information security, with at least 3 in a role where you owned outcomes — CISO, vCISO, Information Security Director, security architect, or senior consultant at an MSSP or advisory firm.
  • You have lived through real incidents. Ransomware, business email compromise, data exfiltration, insider threat, third-party breach. You can talk about what actually happened, what the response cost, and what you would do differently.
  • CISSP, CISM, CCSP, GIAC (GSEC/GCIH/GPEN), or equivalent. Security+ alone is not enough for this role.
  • Fluency across the modern stack — not vendor-deep in one product, but credible in every layer and able to say why one architecture beats another.
  • Framework and compliance fluency you can use in a sales conversation, not just recite: NIST, ISO, CIS, PCI, HIPAA, CMMC, SOX.
  • Working knowledge of cloud — hyperscaler architecture, shared responsibility, and where enterprise cloud transformation creates security gaps.
  • You can whiteboard a defensible architecture live, from memory, in front of a skeptical CISO.

WHAT YOU NEED — SELLING ABILITY

Technical brilliance without commercial instinct will fail in this role.

  • A track record you can prove. Quota attainment, influenced revenue, deals you personally moved. Bring numbers to the interview.
  • Enterprise pre-sales, sales overlay, or direct sales experience. You have been on the hook for a number before, and you liked it.
  • Elite discovery. You ask hard questions in a way that feels like a conversation, not an interrogation, and you can get a CISO to admit what is actually broken.
  • Executive presence. You have presented to boards, CFOs, and CISOs and held the room without hiding behind slides.
  • You sell through, not just to. This is an indirect model. You will win by making a partner look brilliant in front of their own customer, and you have to be genuinely fine with them getting the credit.
  • Business-case thinking. You can frame a security investment in terms of risk reduction, insurance premiums, audit findings, and dollars — not features.
  • Operational discipline. Clean CRM, accurate forecast, multiple concurrent deals, nothing dropped.

WHAT YOU NEED — THE PART WE CARE ABOUT MOST

We can teach the portfolio. We cannot teach this.

  • Self-directed. Nobody is going to tell you what to do every day. We will give you guidance and tools, but you will build a plan in your first two weeks because it did not occur to you to wait.
  • Competitive. You track your own numbers. You know where you rank. Losing a deal to a competitor bothers you for a week.
  • Relentlessly curious. You already read the threat reports, tinker with tools on your own time, and have opinions about where this industry is going.
  • Coachable ego. Confident enough to challenge a CISO, secure enough to be wrong in front of your team.
  • Continuous certification. We require one new industry certification per year and we pay for it. If that sounds like a burden rather than a perk, this is not your role.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Prior experience in the technology advisor / agent channel, a TSD(Technology Solutions Distributor).
  • Existing relationships with security suppliers or channel leadership.
  • Public speaking history — conference stage, podcast, published writing.
  • Offensive security background (pen testing, red team) or deep IR/forensics experience.
  • Experience selling into a specific vertical with heavy compliance pressure — healthcare, finance, defense industrial base, or state and local government.

THIS IS NOT THE RIGHT JOB FOR YOU IF

  • You want to be a pure technical resource with no revenue accountability.
  • You need a full inbound queue to stay busy.
  • You are a single-vendor specialist looking to keep selling that one product.
  • You need the customer relationship to be yours, and it will bother you that it belongs to the partner.
  • You have not touched a live security architecture in three years and are leading with your certifications.

WHO YOU WILL WORK WITH

Supplier channel managers and supplier engineers · Telarus field sales and field support managers · The Telarus Solution Architect and Sales Engineering teams · Technology Advisors, MSPs, and VARs · End customers up to and including the C-suite · Telarus executive leadership

OUR HIRING PROCESS

We designed this to be fast and to be hard. Expect four steps:

  • Screen with the SVP of Sales Engineering — 30 minutes, mostly about your numbers and why you want this.
  • Technical deep-dive with the SE team — real architecture, real tradeoffs, no trivia.
  • Live whiteboard and role-play — we hand you a discovery scenario and a skeptical stakeholder, and you run it. This is the step that decides it.
  • Final with leadership and a supplier reference conversation.
Salary: $150,000-$180,000

We don't sell campaigns — we sell results. And we're growing fast. Unlike traditional lead generation companies, AIM supports clients beyond lead delivery — helping ensure leads are contacted, qualified, and converted into real opportunities. This gives our clients a measurable advantage in speed-to-lead and conversion performance.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Business Development Specialist who understands how to sell performance. As AIM's dedicated sales and business development professional, you'll be responsible for identifying and closing new client partnerships across AIM's target verticals — companies that are serious about lead volume, lead quality, and measurable ROI from their marketing spend.

This isn't a traditional agency sales role. You'll be selling a performance-based model where clients pay for qualified leads, not ad spend — which means you need to understand how to speak credibly to sophisticated buyers about cost-per-lead economics, lead qualification criteria, conversion rates, and ROI. You'll build and manage your own pipeline, lead discovery through close, and serve as the face of AIM in the market.

This role requires more than selling leads — you must understand how leads turn into revenue. You will need to think beyond cost-per-lead and engage prospects in deeper conversations about conversion rates, speed-to-contact, appointment setting, and overall return on marketing investment.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Sales & New Client Acquisition

  • Develop and execute a business development strategy focused on driving new client partnerships for 321 AIM in target verticals: home services, legal services, healthcare, insurance, and financial services
  • Identify and pursue high-value prospects — including regional and national operators, franchise groups, law firms, and healthcare practices — that have strong lead volume needs and are a fit for a performance-based pricing model
  • Lead end-to-end sales cycles from prospecting and discovery through proposal, negotiation, and contract close
  • Conduct discovery conversations that uncover client lead volume goals, cost-per-lead targets, current marketing performance, and qualification criteria — and translate those into a compelling AIM partnership proposal
  • Clearly articulate AIM's value proposition, pricing model, lead qualification standards, and performance expectations to prospects, including C-suite and senior marketing decision-makers
  • Develop customized proposals that outline projected lead volume, qualified-lead definitions, pricing structure, and expected ROI
  • Maintain a disciplined sales pipeline and CRM to track prospect status, activity, and revenue projections
  • Educate prospects on the full lead lifecycle — from lead generation to contact, qualification, and appointment conversion — and position AIM as a partner across that entire funnel
  • Identify opportunities to scale lead volume, expand into additional service areas, or deepen AIM’s role in the client’s acquisition funnel

Market Development & Brand Presence

  • Build AIM's market presence within target verticals through strategic outreach, industry networking, conference participation, and partnership development
  • Identify and cultivate referral relationships with complementary vendors, franchise consultants, industry associations, and channel partners who serve AIM's target client base
  • Monitor competitor offerings, pricing models, and market positioning to ensure AIM's value proposition stays sharp and differentiated
  • Collaborate with AIM leadership to develop sales collateral, case studies, and pitch materials that demonstrate AIM's performance track record and vertical expertise
  • Represent AIM at industry events, trade shows, and vertical-specific conferences relevant to home services, legal, healthcare, insurance, and financial services
  • Diagnose breakdowns in the prospect’s current funnel (e.g., slow response times, poor follow-up, low booking rates) and position AIM as a solution not just for lead volume, but for conversion performance

Client Onboarding & Handoff

  • Serve as the primary point of contact through the pre-onboarding phase, ensuring new clients have a clear understanding of the AIM model, reporting expectations, and lead qualification process
  • Collaborate with AIM's operations and campaign management teams to ensure smooth client onboarding and alignment on qualified-lead definitions, delivery timelines, and performance benchmarks
  • Maintain strong communication during early campaign launch to support client confidence and address questions before transitioning to the ongoing account relationship
  • Identify expansion and upsell opportunities within the existing AIM client base as lead programs scale
  • Ensure alignment between what was sold and how leads will be handled — including intake process, response expectations, and appointment-setting workflows

WHAT YOU HAVE

  • 3+ years of experience in business development, sales, or client acquisition — with direct experience selling performance marketing, lead generation, or pay-per-lead programs strongly preferred
  • Deep understanding of performance-based pricing models: cost-per-lead, cost-per-acquisition, lead qualification standards, and the economics of lead generation programs
  • Proven track record of meeting and exceeding revenue and new client acquisition targets
  • Experience selling into at least one of AIM's core verticals — home services, legal services, healthcare, insurance, or financial services — is a significant plus
  • Strong command of lead generation strategy, digital media fundamentals, and the ability to speak credibly to clients about campaign mechanics, attribution, and ROI
  • Exceptional discovery and consultative selling skills — you ask the right questions, listen well, and build proposals that directly address client business goals
  • Excellent negotiation skills with the ability to navigate complex contracts, performance guarantees, and qualified-lead definition discussions
  • Proficiency in CRM platforms, pipeline management, and sales automation tools
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to develop and deliver compelling sales presentations to senior executives
  • Self-directed, entrepreneurial, and comfortable operating in a fast-growing, performance-driven environment
  • Experience selling complex or consultative solutions
  • Ability to understand and communicate full-funnel performance metrics, including lead-to-contact rate, appointment set rate, and revenue impact
  • Experience running structured discovery that uncovers both marketing and operational gaps

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

  • New client revenue closed (monthly/quarterly)
  • Pipeline creation and conversion rates
  • Average deal size and contract value
  • Client retention and early performance success
  • Expansion revenue from existing accounts

REPORTING STRUCTURE

The Business Development Specialist reports directly to 321 AIM leadership and works in close coordination with AIM's operations and campaign management teams. This role operates as a standalone business development function with direct visibility to senior leadership and significant influence over AIM's growth trajectory.

COMPENSATION

Structure: Competitive base salary + uncapped commission + performance-based bonuses

Compensation is structured to reward performance. Commission is uncapped and tied directly to new client revenue closed. Performance bonuses apply to volume milestones and client retention benchmarks. Top performers in this role have significant earning upside tied directly to AIM's growth. Top performers in this role have the potential to earn [optional: realistic OTE range] by consistently closing and expanding high-value client partnerships.

321 AIM BENEFITS

  • 100% remote work environment
  • Flexible scheduling with core collaboration hours
  • Paid time off + company-observed holidays
  • Health, dental, and vision benefits
  • Professional development budget and industry conference attendance
  • Direct access to AIM leadership and a fast-moving, performance-obsessed team
  • Uncapped earning potential tied to a genuinely differentiated product in a high-demand market
Salary: Competitive base salary + commission and bonuses

raw.description:
Who We Are

Right Hook Digital is a growth marketing agency working with 7-8 figure DTC eCommerce brands across the US and Australia. We're a Premium Google and Meta Marketing Partner, a global team of 60+, and we're scaling our US retention business.

We've partnered with brands like Alpha Lion, July Luggage, Geedup, Mister Zimi, Silly George, and many more. Our work spans paid social, Google, and retention - and we take all three seriously.

At our core, we're a team of A-Players who genuinely care about outcomes. We've built a culture around Kaizen (continuous growth), openness and candor, and elevating one another - and we look for people who live those values, not just nod at them.

The Role

We're looking for a Head of Retention to own our Retention service line end to end - the P&L, the product, the people, and the client relationships that hold it all together.

This is a business leadership role, not a senior IC role. You won't be building flows in Klaviyo. You'll be building the team that builds them, the product that makes them world-class, and the commercial engine that turns both into profitable growth.

You'll lead Group Leaders, Retention Strategists, and Specialists. You'll be the escalation point our biggest retention clients trust. And you'll own the number: gross profit growth in the Retention service line.

If you've run a service line or department before, know lifecycle marketing deeply enough to raise the standard of the work, and get real satisfaction from developing people - this is a rare seat.

What You'll Own

P&L Accountability

  • Own the Retention department's P&L and hit gross profit targets, quarter after quarter
  • Monitor department performance metrics - average client lifetime, churn, retention rates - and act early when they move the wrong way
  • Make the resourcing and pricing calls that protect margin without compromising the work

Product Excellence

  • Keep the Retention product world-class, generating genuine mutual upside for clients
  • Own "The Retention Way" - our core system - including documentation, training, SOP adherence, and the tie-breaking decisions on how it evolves
  • Push innovation in lifecycle strategy, testing, and measurement so we stay ahead of what every other agency is selling

Client Relationships

  • Build and hold strong relationships with our key retention clients, and serve as the primary escalation point when things get hard
  • Drive retention by supporting and guiding Strategists on campaigns and flows that actually move revenue
  • Proactively hunt for client feedback, aiming to WOW rather than satisfy
  • Run exit interviews with churned clients and feed what you learn back into the product

People Leadership

  • Hire, develop, and - when needed - exit talent, with a clear eye on who can make a meaningful impact on P&L growth
  • Act as an S-leader to Group Leaders, Strategists, and Specialists
  • Use our Performance and Growth Framework (PGF) to run consistent 1:1s, PGP reviews, KPI reviews, and feedback loops that people genuinely value

Growth & Operational Excellence

  • Work with our marketing team on agency campaigns, marketing materials, case studies, testimonials, and lead generation for Retention
  • Support sales conversations where your expertise closes the gap
  • Build strong relationships with our Paid Social and Google units to drive internal referrals
  • Partner with the Process Excellence Manager and COO to lift utilization, billable income, and process efficiency

Who You Are

  • You've led a retention, lifecycle, or CRM team - ideally in an agency, and ideally with P&L or revenue accountability
  • You know email and SMS deeply. You don't need to be the fastest person in Klaviyo, but you need to know world-class work from adequate work in about ten seconds, and be able to explain the difference
  • You've managed teams, not just individual contributors
  • You're commercially fluent - gross profit, utilization, retention rates and pricing are tools you use, not concepts you've heard of
  • You're comfortable being the escalation point. Hard client conversations don't rattle you
  • You give and receive candid feedback well. Our culture runs on openness, and a leader who softens everything won't work here
  • You default to systems. When something breaks twice, you fix the process, not just the instance
  • You're happy working overlapping US hours in a globally distributed team

Bonus points for: experience with 7-8 figure DTC brands, hands-on Klaviyo history, a track record building or productising a service offering, or experience supporting sales and marketing as a subject matter expert.

Why This Role

You're inheriting a real business with real clients and a team already doing good work - not a blank page and not a mess. Retention is one of three service lines we take equally seriously, which means you'll have the investment and the internal referral pipeline to grow it, plus the autonomy to shape how.

You'll report directly to our COO and sit at the table where the decisions get made.

  • May specialize /certify in one or more Industry Segments.
  • Acts as a change advocate, and is open to new and different ways of thinking.
  • Communication (verbal and written) - Interacts and communicates with confidence with all levels of external and/or internal business partners within scope of responsibility, team and/or matrix environment. Can judge appropriate means and method to communicate based on the nature of the communication. Able to influence desired outcomes to drive actions and results. Adept at influencing even when holding a position contrary to the majority opinion.
  • Judgement and Decision Making - Ability to exercise judgment, negotiate and make sound business decisions based on level of authority. Applies judgment and expertise to determine when escalation is needed. Demonstrates confidence in one’s ability to apply decision making to UW assessment.

Is able to engage multiple members of a group to share information and to consider other points of view to reach objectives, consensus and/or deadlines.

Acts as a mentor for less experienced underwriters or newly hired underwriters, may assist with training other team members. About the Role

IAA is seeking a Principal Data Engineer to serve as the most senior individual contributor and technical authority across our data engineering function. This is a hands-on, deeply technical leadership role for an engineer who sets architectural direction, raises the engineering bar, and personally builds the most complex and business-critical components of IAA’s data platform.

Where the Director leads through people and strategy, the Principal Data Engineer leads through technical depth, influence, and execution. This person defines patterns and standards, solves the hardest data engineering problems, and acts as a force multiplier for engineers across the organization. They ensure IAA’s data platform is scalable, reliable, secure, and ready to power advanced analytics, BI, forecasting, and the data needs of AI solutions.

This is a high-visibility role that partners closely with engineering leadership, data scientists, BI developers, platform/infrastructure teams, and business stakeholders across Operations, Sales, Marketing, and Product.

What You’ll Do

  • Set and evolve the technical architecture for IAA’s data platform — ingestion, transformation, storage, semantic modeling, and data delivery — on the Azure data and analytics stack.
  • Personally design and build the most complex, high-impact data pipelines, frameworks, and reusable components that other engineers build upon.
  • Define engineering standards and patterns across architecture, code quality, performance, scalability, observability, and governance — and drive their adoption through example and mentorship.
  • Lead the design and implementation of robust pipelines, semantic models, and data products that power dashboards, self-service analytics, forecasting, and downstream machine learning systems.
  • Build the production-grade data pipelines and feature/data infrastructure that data scientists rely on to train, serve, and operationalize models.
  • Diagnose and resolve the toughest performance, reliability, and scalability challenges across BI and data workloads (e.g., Power BI, Synapse, Fabric).
  • Drive technical strategy and execution across Microsoft Fabric, Synapse, Power BI, and broader Azure BI technologies, evaluating new tools and making build/buy recommendations.
  • Mentor and grow data engineers and analytics engineers, conducting design reviews and elevating the technical capability of the team.

Summary

SafetyChain Software is looking for a Senior Business Development Representative (BDR) to join our Sales team.This is a senior/tenured position within our BDR team. In addition to core pipeline generation, this person will take on an informal team lead role, surfacing team progress and blockers to the BDR Manager, helping keep the broader team aligned, while still carrying a full individual quota.

We're building a team that operates at the cutting edge, our BDRs are expected to actively use AI tools to research accounts, build better outreach, and find creative ways to generate pipeline faster. If you've figured out how to use AI to work smarter and do more, you'll fit right in here.

About Us:

SafetyChain is a rapidly scaling B2B SaaS provider revolutionizing plant management for Food and Beverage manufacturers by improving yield, maximizing productivity, and ensuring compliance. Our impressive client base includes renowned brands like Albertsons, Clif Bar, Tyson Foods, and Whole Foods. Join a dynamic, collaborative team driven by innovation, agility, and rapid growth.

We are a remote-first company. While this role is primarily remote, there may be occasional opportunities to collaborate in person for quarterly business reviews, team training, or customer visits. This is completely optional and flexible based on your location and preferences.

Key Responsibilities:

The Senior Business Development Representative (BDR) will play a critical role in moving prospective buyers through the sales funnel. You will engage with inbound leads—primarily Marketing Qualified Leads (MQLs)—as well as manage recycled leads and re-engagement opportunities. Your focus will be to qualify prospects, nurture early interest, and set high-quality appointments for our Account Executives.

Team Lead Support: act as a point of contact between the BDR team and BDR Manager, surfacing activity trends, blockers, and wins Mentorship: help onboard and coach newer BDRs on process, tools, and best practices

  • Lead Engagement
  • Lead Management
  • Qualification
  • Own small projects that support pipeline generation
  • Relationship Building
  • Top-of-Funnel Excellence
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Problem Solving
  • Continuous Learning

Performance Expectations

  • Activity Targets: Approximately 40–50 outreach activities (calls, emails, LinkedIn touches) per day.
  • SQL Goal: Aim to generate 12–16 qualified sales opportunities per month.
  • Speed-to-Lead: Initial outreach to inbound leads within 24 hours.
  • We’ll provide the tools, training, and support to help you hit these numbers confidently.

Qualifications:

  • Have 2+ years of BDR/SDR or equivalent sales development experience, with a demonstrated track record of hitting or exceeding quota, preferably within the B2B/Saas or enterprise software industry.
  • Comfortable taking on informal leadership responsibilities — communicating team progress to management and supporting teammates without formal authority.
  • Willing to experiment with new tools and approaches to find what generates pipeline.
  • Comfortable experimenting with AI tools to improve outreach quality and efficiency
  • Have strong organizational and time management skills—you can keep moving even when managing a high volume of leads.
  • Are a self-starter who’s motivated to succeed in sales and open to feedback along the way.
  • Communicate clearly, listen actively, and can build rapport with all kinds of people.
  • Are comfortable learning and using tools like Sales Navigator, HubSpot, and other tools.
  • Are a natural problem solver who stays proactive and focuses on results.
  • Are eager to learn, grow, multi-task, and take on new challenges. We invest in our people.
  • Experience informally leading, mentoring, or supporting peers is a plus.

Growth Path: This role is designed as a stepping stone. High performers can expect a path into a full-time BDR Manager or Account Executive role within 12-18 months.

Why Join Us?

At SafetyChain Solutions, we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being and professional growth:

  • Health & Wellness: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance plans to keep you and your family healthy.
  • Retirement Planning: A 401(k) plan with company matching to help you save for the future.
  • Work-Life Balance: Unlimited paid time off (PTO) and holidays to ensure you have time to recharge.
  • Professional Development: Opportunities for continuous learning, including access to training resources, workshops, and conferences.
  • Flexible Work Environment: Fully Remote with a generous monthly home office payment.
  • Employee Engagement: Regular team-building activities, company events, and an inclusive work culture that values diversity and collaboration.

Personal Attributes We Value

  • Experimentalism: you're willing to test new tools, sequences, and tactics without needing perfect conditions to get started. You learn by doing, debrief honestly, and apply it fast.
  • Initiative: you are a scrappy, self-motivated go-getter with the ability to accept and incorporate coaching and feedback.
  • Collaborative: you seek opportunities to learn from others, solicit honest feedback and always have the best interests of the team and our customers in mind.
  • Inquisitiveness: a desire to expand your knowledge base and explore concepts and ideas that are new and unfamiliar.
  • Process Driven: you are highly structured, disciplined and organized in creating and executing operational processes to ensure a consistent, repeatable outcome.
  • Integrity: you do what you say you will do and don’t let your colleagues or customers down.
  • Patience: the ability to adapt to changing situations while remaining calm, collected, and committed.
  • Self-improvement: the ability to identify mistakes and quickly adjust approach when confronted with new information or perspective.

Equal Opportunity Employer: All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, marital status, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law applicable to the state in which you work

Hisense is one of the world’s fastest-growing consumer electronics and home appliance brands, delivering televisions, Laser TV, refrigeration, laundry, and air solutions to millions of households. Locations:Remote (US) with positions in several regions: California, Upper Midwest, Great Lakes/Ohio Valley, Northeast, and Southeast with occasional travel to Alpharetta, GA office

Job Overview:

The Regional Manager plays a pivotal role in enhancing Hisense’s presence within Best Buy stores by guiding and supporting the Best Buy employees funded by Hisense. This is leadership without a badge of authority: the specialists you develop don’t report to you, so your influence, coaching, and credibility are what turn training into product knowledge, product knowledge into better customer conversations, and better conversations into Hisense TV and soundbar sales.

You are the face of Hisense in your region’s stores — on the road 60–70% of the time, assessing execution, coaching specialists, building relationships with Best Buy store and market leadership, and feeding what you see on the floor back to the Retail Operations team.

Duties/Responsibilities:

  • Team development: Provide guidance, training, and ongoing support to Hisense-funded Best Buy teams to optimize sales of Hisense TVs and soundbars.
  • Indirect leadership: Influence without direct authority — aligning specialists and store teams with Hisense’s sales strategies, priorities, and standards.
  • Store visits: Conduct regular store visits across your region to assess performance, deliver coaching, influence product placement and merchandising compliance, and implement development plans.
  • Performance management: Monitor KPIs for product knowledge, sales techniques, and customer engagement; track and report on team progress, training effectiveness, and sales outcomes.
  • Partner collaboration: Collaborate with Best Buy store and market management and Hisense internal teams to resolve issues and identify opportunities; serve as the voice of the specialist back to Hisense leadership.
  • Regional planning: Develop and execute regional action plans to boost product visibility, display compliance, and sales performance.
  • Compliance: Ensure compliance with company policies, program requirements, and retail best practices.

Requirements/Qualifications:

  • Minimum of 6 years of multi-unit retail management experience; proven retail background required, consumer electronics highly desirable but not mandatory.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the demonstrated ability to influence and motivate teams you don’t directly manage.
  • Willingness to travel extensively (60–70%) across the assigned region; valid driver’s license and reliable transportation required.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and sales tracking tools.
  • Ability to work independently in a fast-paced, field-based environment.
  • College degree in Business, Marketing, or a related field preferred but not required.

Preferred Skills:

  • Experience in vendor-funded retail programs or partnerships.
  • Knowledge of TV and audio product categories.

Hisense USA offers competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k), paid time off, and employee product discounts.

ZeroFox protects what's real by removing what isn't. We steadfastly safeguard organizations from fraud, abuse, misinformation, and attack by preemptively exposing, disrupting, and eliminating external threats across the public attack surface — because when people can't tell what's real, they stop trusting everything.

ZeroFox uniquely fuses Cyber Threat Intelligence, Brand and Domain Protection, Attack Surface Intelligence, Executive Protection, and Physical Security Intelligence in one platform packed with intelligence you'll actually use. Our continuous cycle — Discover, Validate, Disrupt — helps thousands of customers worldwide, including leaders in finance, media, technology, retail, healthcare, and government, reduce risk, accelerate response, and defend their world.

We're growing fast, investing deeply in AI, and building a team of people who are serious about results and never take themselves too seriously. If you're ready to take the fight to the adversary, come defend your world with us.

WHAT ZEROFOX WILL LOOK LIKE TO YOU

Commercial is where ZeroFox's enterprise sales motion is growing fastest. You'll be selling into mid-market and commercial accounts that have real security exposure and are actively looking for a platform that does what ZeroFox does — most of them just haven't met us yet. This is a full-cycle AE role with a warm pipeline from a coordinated SDR team and a product that gives you something genuine to say on every call.

You'll own a TOLA commercial territory end-to-end — sourcing, running, and closing deals with mid-market buyers across ZeroFox's core verticals. Your deals will range from $30K to $150K+ ARR, and you'll be working alongside SDRs, channel partners, and solutions engineers to get them across the line. The accounts you're selling into have real problems: phishing infrastructure targeting their customers, executive impersonation, brand abuse. Your job is to connect that reality to what ZeroFox actually does. In your first 90 days, you'll complete product and process onboarding, co-sell two to three deals with a senior AE, and build your first territory plan.

YOU'LL THRIVE HERE IF...

  • You've closed B2B SaaS deals in the $30K–$150K range and can walk through your sales process without prompting

THIS PROBABLY ISN'T FOR YOU IF...

  • You need a highly structured inbound-heavy environment to be productive — this role requires consistent self-directed prospecting

WOULD LOVE, BUT WE WON'T HOLD IT AGAINST YOU:

Every day, the world's most mission-critical companies — banks, hospitals, governments, and Fortune 500 enterprises — run on Salesforce. Five years from now, you'll look back at a category you helped define — and an enterprise software movement you helped lead.

Cold Email Outreach Specialist (Outbound Email & Lead Generation) – Remote

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Location: Middle East Preferred
Working Hours: U.S. Client Business Hours

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a Cold Email Outreach Specialist to generate qualified sales opportunities through strategic outbound email campaigns.

This is a hands-on, performance-driven role where you’ll own the entire cold email process—from building targeted prospect lists and writing personalized outreach to managing deliverability, optimizing campaigns, and qualifying inbound responses.

Success in this role comes from combining strong copywriting, technical deliverability knowledge, and a data-driven approach to consistently generate qualified pipeline for the sales team.

If you’re passionate about outbound prospecting, enjoy experimenting with messaging, and understand what it takes to keep campaigns landing in inboxes—not spam folders—this role is for you.

What You’ll Own

Prospect Research & List Building

  • Build highly targeted prospect lists using:
    • Apollo
    • ZoomInfo
    • LinkedIn Sales Navigator
    • Crunchbase
    • Similar prospecting platforms
  • Segment prospects by:
    • Industry
    • Company size
    • Job title
    • Geography
    • Ideal Customer Profile (ICP)
  • Verify and clean contact data using:
    • NeverBounce
    • ZeroBounce
    • Clearout
  • Maintain organized prospect databases and outreach lists.

Cold Email Campaign Management

  • Write personalized cold email copy, subject lines, and calls-to-action.
  • Build and launch multi-step outbound sequences (4–8 touchpoints).
  • Personalize messaging using company and prospect research.
  • Monitor campaign performance daily.
  • Continuously optimize campaigns based on engagement and reply metrics.

Deliverability & Inbox Management

  • Manage inbox reputation using platforms such as:
    • Instantly
    • Lemlist
    • Smartlead
    • Mailwarm
  • Monitor:
    • Bounce rates
    • Spam scores
    • Sender reputation
    • Inbox health
  • Rotate sending domains and inboxes to maximize deliverability.
  • Identify and resolve deliverability issues before campaign performance declines.

Campaign Optimization & Reporting

  • Conduct A/B testing on:
    • Subject lines
    • Messaging
    • CTAs
    • Send times
  • Track key metrics including:
    • Open rates
    • Positive reply rates
    • Bounce rates
    • Conversion rates
  • Prepare campaign performance reports and recommend improvements.
  • Document testing results and optimization history.

Lead Qualification & CRM Management

  • Review campaign replies and categorize responses accurately.
  • Identify qualified prospects and route them to the sales team.
  • Maintain accurate CRM records using:
    • HubSpot
    • Salesforce
    • Zoho CRM
    • Similar CRM platforms
  • Ensure outreach data remains organized and up to date.

Compliance & Best Practices

  • Ensure campaigns comply with:
    • CAN-SPAM
    • GDPR
    • CCPA
  • Maintain suppression and unsubscribe lists.
  • Follow outbound email best practices to protect sender reputation.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • Excellent persuasive and concise writing skills.
  • Strong analytical mindset with a focus on performance improvement.
  • Comfortable using outbound automation and deliverability tools.
  • Organized, proactive, and highly execution-focused.
  • Strong attention to detail.
  • Continuously tests, learns, and optimizes campaign performance.

Required Experience & Skills

Experience

  • 1–2+ years of experience in:
    • Cold Email Outreach
    • Outbound Lead Generation
    • Sales Development (SDR)
    • Outbound Marketing

Technical Skills

  • Hands-on experience with:
    • Apollo
    • Instantly
    • Lemlist
    • Smartlead
    • Woodpecker
    • Similar outreach platforms
  • Experience writing cold email campaigns.
  • Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills.
  • Excellent written English communication.

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience managing large-scale email deliverability.
  • Understanding of:
    • DNS
    • SPF
    • DKIM
    • DMARC
  • Experience supporting B2B SaaS, agencies, or service businesses.
  • Experience collaborating with SDRs or Account Executives.
  • Familiarity with outbound automation workflows and CRM integrations.

What a Typical Day Looks Like

  • Build and refine prospect lists.
  • Launch and monitor outbound email campaigns.
  • Review inbox health and deliverability metrics.
  • Optimize messaging, targeting, and campaign performance.
  • Qualify interested prospects and hand them off to sales.
  • Update CRM records and maintain campaign documentation.

In short: You own outbound email execution—from research and personalization to optimization and lead qualification—ensuring a consistent flow of qualified opportunities into the sales pipeline.

Key Metrics for Success (KPIs)

  • High email open rates.
  • Positive reply and conversation rates.
  • Low bounce rates and strong inbox health.
  • Consistent campaign execution and optimization.
  • Accurate CRM documentation.
  • Growth in qualified outbound pipeline.

Why Join Us?

  • Own the complete outbound email process from strategy to execution.
  • Work with modern sales engagement and automation tools.
  • Directly influence pipeline growth and revenue generation.
  • Performance-driven environment with measurable impact.
  • Opportunities to grow into:
    • Senior Outbound Specialist
    • Sales Development Team Lead
    • Outbound Growth Manager
    • Revenue Operations

Interview Process

  1. Initial Phone Screen
  2. Spark Hire Intro Video (3–5 minutes)
  3. Recruiter Interview
  4. Practical Assessment (Cold Email Sequence Exercise)
  5. Client Interview
  6. Offer & Onboarding

What Happens After You Apply

Right after you apply, you’ll receive an email invitation from Spark Hire to record your Intro Video. This short, self-recorded video is the next step that completes your application and can be recorded whenever it’s convenient for you.

Instead of repeating yourself across multiple screening calls, you’ll introduce yourself once, and your video will be shared with the hiring team. This helps the hiring team evaluate your communication style early, making future interviews more meaningful while reducing unnecessary interview rounds.

Don’t overthink it—you can record your video as many times as you’d like before submitting it. Only your final submission will be reviewed.

Please keep an eye on both your inbox and spam folder for your Spark Hire invitation after submitting your application.

Apply Now

If you’re passionate about outbound prospecting, enjoy writing high-performing cold emails, understand email deliverability, and want to help generate qualified sales opportunities through data-driven outreach, we’d love to hear from you. Apply today and become a key contributor to building a predictable outbound pipeline.

Skills Coach – Level 5 People Professional Apprenticeship

Contract: Full-time

Location: Remote, UK. Candidates must live within reasonable travelling distance of London for occasional in-person days

Start Date: Immediate start available

Closing Date: Monday 10th August 2026

(We may close this advert early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications. We encourage early applications.)

Join KnowledgeBrief

KnowledgeBrief is a leadership and management training provider specialising in apprenticeships, leadership development, business competency training and professional skills development.

Through digital learning, workshops, coaching and practical development programmes, we help individuals and organisations build the knowledge, confidence and capabilities they need to succeed.

We are a values-driven organisation focused on innovation, authenticity, inspiration and strong relationships, creating meaningful impact for our learners, clients and colleagues.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced coaching professional to support learners completing our Level 5 People Professional Apprenticeship.

This is primarily a coaching and pastoral role. You will build trusted relationships with learners, help them overcome barriers and provide the right balance of support, encouragement and constructive challenge. Working with learners, line managers and the wider Apprenticeship Team, you will help learners remain engaged, take ownership of their progress and apply their learning within real HR and workplace situations.

You do not need to be a senior HR specialist, but you must be confident working with HR and people professionals and understanding their workplace context.

The role is fully remote, although candidates must live within reasonable travelling distance of London for occasional meetings and company events.

Key Responsibilities

You will:

  • Provide expert coaching, guidance and motivation to adult learners enrolled on the Level 5 People Professional Apprenticeship
  • Develop tailored learning plans that support progression from each learner’s individual starting point
  • Integrate on-the-job and off-the-job learning, helping learners apply people practices effectively
  • Provide additional support and catch-up strategies based on individual learner needs
  • Engage line managers in learner progress through regular tripartite reviews
  • Prepare learners for end-point assessment
  • Ensure learners meet off-the-job training requirements and achieve their learning outcomes
  • Proactively re-engage learners who are falling behind and support them to return to planned progress
  • Maintain accurate and timely learner records in line with funding, quality and compliance requirements
  • Support with Workshop delivery and marking
  • Participate in Apprenticeship Team and standardisation meetings
  • Foster a passion for learning among professionals from a diverse range of organisations and industries

Experience, Skills & Qualifications

Essential

  • Experience coaching, mentoring or supporting adult learners
  • A strong pastoral approach and the ability to respond appropriately to barriers affecting learning
  • The ability to build trusted relationships while maintaining clear expectations and accountability
  • Confidence holding supportive and appropriately challenging conversations
  • Strong communication, organisation and learner-management skills
  • Confidence working with HR and people professionals and helping them apply learning in the workplace
  • A relevant qualification in coaching, teaching, assessing, learning and development or people practice, or equivalent professional experience
  • An understanding of safeguarding and effective learner support

Desirable

  • Experience within the apprenticeship or further education sector
  • Experience supporting Level 5 People Professional learners
  • Knowledge of apprenticeship requirements, including off-the-job training and end-point assessment
  • A recognised coaching, teaching or assessing qualification
  • A Level 5 or higher qualification in coaching, learning and development, HR or people practice

Interpersonal Fit

We’re looking for someone who:

  • Is warm, approachable and committed to providing a positive learner experience
  • Brings curiosity and a passion for learning
  • Communicates clearly and builds strong relationships
  • Balances empathy with constructive challenge and accountability
  • Takes ownership, works collaboratively and delivers with quality

Why Work With Us?

At KnowledgeBrief, we are committed to creating an environment where people feel supported, challenged and able to grow.

You’ll benefit from:

  • Dedicated monthly CPD time
  • 5.6 weeks’ annual leave plus bank holidays
  • Two-week company closure over Christmas and New Year
  • Company sick pay
  • Access to our Employee Assistance Programme and wellbeing support
  • Opportunities to contribute to cross-team projects and organisational growth
  • A remote-first environment with opportunities to connect in person

Our Commitment to Safer Recruitment and Inclusion

KnowledgeBrief is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of learners, and all colleagues are expected to share this commitment.

Offers of employment are subject to pre-employment checks, including right to work, references and DBS checks where appropriate.

We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from all backgrounds. Reasonable adjustments are available throughout the recruitment process.

Application Process

  • Submit your CV via our dedicated platform
  • Initial screening with the People & Culture Team
  • Interview stage or stages with the hiring team
  • Final decision and feedback

We aim to keep the process timely, transparent and respectful of your experience.

Ready to Apply?

If this opportunity aligns with your experience and aspirations, we would love to hear from you.

Please submit your CV and we will be in touch.

The Hiring Team

KnowledgeBrief
